topLine: With the 2027 state election drawing closer, the day's running theme was nerves inside NSW Labor: the Sydney Morning Herald reports some of the party's advertising is leaning heavily on Premier Chris Minns as polling slides, while the Australian Financial Review reports Labor MPs are hearing voter anger about federal issues on the doorstep. Minns also cut a press conference short after being heckled by Greens candidate Shane Bazzi, an incident the Greens have rebuked. On policy, the government announced a modern slavery taskforce and a rollout of free ADHD assessments, while the Tenants' Union pressed for rental bond interest to fund the state's rental taskforce.

briefing.topLine: With the 2027 state election drawing closer, the day's running theme was nerves inside NSW Labor: the Sydney Morning Herald reports some of the party's advertising is leaning heavily on Premier Chris Minns as polling slides, while the Australian Financial Review reports Labor MPs are hearing voter anger about federal issues on the doorstep. Minns also cut a press conference short after being heckled by Greens candidate Shane Bazzi, an incident the Greens have rebuked. On policy, the government announced a modern slavery taskforce and a rollout of free ADHD assessments, while the Tenants' Union pressed for rental bond interest to fund the state's rental taskforce.
briefing.localWatch: Locally it was a quiet day: Kiama Council reports its motion on filling casual councillor vacancies has been endorsed, and Shoalhaven City Council has opened consultation on making the Nowra CBD safer and more inclusive.

stories.headline: Kiama’s motion on casual councillor vacancies gets green light
stories.summary: Kiama Council reports that a motion it brought forward dealing with casual councillor vacancies has been supported. No further detail is given in the council's notice.

stories.headline: Your voice can help create a safer and more inclusive Nowra CBD
stories.summary: Shoalhaven City Council is inviting community input on making the Nowra CBD safer and more inclusive, according to the council's news release.

stories.headline: Greens rebuke candidate Shane Bazzi after he crashed Chris Minns press conference
stories.summary: The Australian reports the Greens have rebuked their candidate Shane Bazzi after he disrupted a press conference held by Premier Chris Minns. The Daily Telegraph reports Bazzi chanted at the Premier and made accusations against him, and 7NEWS reports Minns ended the press conference early because of the disruption.

stories.headline: Australian MP proposes to partner during speech in NSW state parliament – video
stories.summary: The Guardian reports that Jordan Lane, the outgoing Liberal member for Ryde, closed his valedictory speech in the Legislative Assembly by proposing to his partner, Natalie.

stories.headline: New taskforce to crack down on modern slavery
stories.summary: The Minns government says it will convene a taskforce to crack down on modern slavery. The ABC reports that as the taskforce was announced, Woolworths disclosed that its own supply chain scrutiny led to about $100,000 in payments being returned to workers in its fruit and vegetable supply chains.

stories.headline: NSW Police shortfall hits record 2704 officers as urgent call-outs surge 72 per cent
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports the NSW Police officer shortfall has reached a record 2704 positions, with urgent call-outs up 72 per cent, and that frontline ranks have shrunk while deskbound roles have grown.

stories.headline: NSW renters' bonds could generate $200m a year to help tenants, union says
stories.summary: The ABC reports the NSW Tenants' Union argues that accruing interest on rental bonds could raise about $200 million to boost funding for the state's rental taskforce.

stories.headline: 'Still waiting for answers': loss of Newcastle reproductive rights shaping as election issue
stories.summary: The Newcastle Herald reports Hunter unions are pressing the NSW government to set out where patients will be able to access IVF and other reproductive services once Newcastle Private Hospital stops providing them under the pending Calvary Health Care takeover. The paper frames the issue as shaping up as an election matter.

stories.headline: ‘More Box Hills’: Councils warn levy changes would create suburbs without footpaths
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports councils have warned that proposed changes to development levies would result in new suburbs lacking basic infrastructure such as footpaths.

stories.headline: Free ADHD diagnoses now rolling out across NSW
stories.summary: The government says free ADHD assessments are now available at 15 GP clinics across NSW, with more clinics to come online in coming months as part of the Minns government's reforms.

stories.headline: Sydney MP retracts state funeral suggestion for ex-colleague after backlash
stories.summary: The ABC reports independent MP Alex Greenwich has apologised after suggesting a state funeral for the late Fred Nile, with Premier Chris Minns saying the state does not have "the resources" to hold a state funeral for every prominent figure.

stories.headline: ‘Gamble’: NSW attacks Bowen on carbon credits
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports a NSW attack on Bowen over carbon credits, with the approach described in the headline as a "gamble". No further detail is available in the supplied text.

stories.headline: Minns warning to offshore bosses behind livestreamed violence
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports Premier Chris Minns has warned overseas-based figures the paper links to the funding of livestreamed street violence in Sydney that they are "not out of reach forever".

stories.headline: Ribbon cut on The Hills’ first public preschool ahead of Gables Public School opening next year
stories.summary: The government has opened the first public preschool in The Hills district ahead of the Gables Public School opening next year, framing it as part of its school infrastructure program in Sydney's north-west.

stories.headline: Why a project that breaches height limits by 400 per cent could be approved
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports a proposed driving range at Port Kembla Golf Club, which the paper says breaches height limits by 400 per cent, has been recommended for approval and will go before the Wollongong Local Planning Panel.

stories.headline: Could the Greens hurt Labor with their preferences in New South Wales?
stories.summary: Ben Raue examines preference flows in NSW, writing that at recent elections preferences have tended to favour Labor, and that this holds even under the state's optional preferential voting system. He explores what would change if Greens preferences behaved differently.

stories.headline: One Some or All: Optional Preferential Voting at the 2023 NSW Election
stories.summary: Antony Green writes that he is preparing a research publication on optional preferential voting for the NSW Parliamentary Research Service, and sets out analysis of how voters used one, some or all preferences at the 2023 state election.

stories.headline: Team Chris Minns: As Labor’s popularity dives, NSW candidates lean on premier
stories.summary: The Herald reports that with polls showing a slide in Anthony Albanese's standing with voters, some NSW Labor campaign material built around the Premier has raised eyebrows inside the party.

stories.headline: ‘They’re having an Albo rant’: Voter anger has NSW Labor MPs worried
stories.summary: The AFR reports NSW Labor MPs are concerned about voter anger directed at the federal government being carried into state politics.

stories.headline: Bankstown or Blacktown? Labor follows Kellie Sloane’s broken map of western Sydney
stories.summary: The Herald's CBD column notes that a year after Opposition Leader Kellie Sloane confused two key western Sydney suburbs, Labor MLC Mark Buttigieg has made the same mix-up.

elsewhere.text: The ABC reports Victorian Labor is facing what it describes as a potentially catastrophic election result, with federal colleagues keeping their distance from the campaign.
The Newcastle Herald reports Labor's campaign is being blamed as the party faces a defeat it says could be costlier than when Jeff Kennett first became premier.
In the AFR, analysis argues Victorian Labor leader Ben Carroll has been unable to shed the legacy of predecessors Daniel Andrews and Jacinta Allan.
Crikey's deep dive into the Victorian seat of Prahran looks at a Liberal-held electorate where the Greens are competitive — a reminder of how three-cornered contests play out.
